# [redacted-project]  Personal quote library app for **iOS and macOS** — SwiftUI + SwiftData + Apple Foundation Models. Multiplatform single target (`#if os`, not Catalyst); shared CloudKit + App Group store syncs iPhone ↔ Mac.  ## Build (iOS)  ```bash xcodebuild -project [redacted-project].xcodeproj -scheme [redacted-project] -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=E05F1A8B-A37A-4699-B609-937FF582777C' build ```
Simulator: iPhone 17 Pro, id `E05F1A8B-A37A-4699-B609-937FF582777C` (iOS 27.0 runtime; the older `3A57B2A9…` id is unavailable since the 26.5 runtime was removed). Note: simulator UDIDs change when the OS updates — if the destination isn't found, run `xcrun simctl list devices` to get the current iPhone 17 Pro id.  ### Schemes (the `dev-build-*` CLI recipe reads this)  The project-agnostic CLI build recipe (`dev-build-sim-installed` → step 3 `cli` branch) resolves the **dev sim scheme** from this section.  | Scheme | Use | |--------|-----| | `[redacted-project]` | The iOS app — dev sim **builds** (tests run via Xcode MCP, see below). Bundle id `com.example.[redacted-project]`, product `[redacted-project].app`. | | `quotewidgetExtension` | Widget extension. |
| `share` | Share extension. |  **Dev sim scheme: `[redacted-project]`.** Unlike [redacted-project], [redacted-project] has **no backend** (SwiftData + CloudKit; only read-only Wikiquote/Wikipedia/Google Books enrichment) → **no local/remote split and no machine rule** — `[redacted-project]` is the dev sim scheme on every host. (For macOS, do **not** use the CLI — see below.)  ## Tests — CLI `xcodebuild test` works  The shared `[redacted-project]` scheme's Test action includes `[redacted-project]Tests` (`[redacted-project]UITests` is not in it — [redacted-project]#58). Run the unit suite from the CLI: add `-only-testing:[redacted-project]Tests test` (and `-parallel-testing-enabled NO` for stable runs) to the build command above. Validated 2026-09-29 by four generator/evaluator runs. The Xcode MCP (`RunAllTests`/`RunSomeTests`) also works when the project is open. Known: full runs hit Core Data `No eligible connection available` crashes ([redacted-project]#55) when the simulator carries stale state or is still booting. Fix confirmed 2026-09-30 across four full runs: `xcrun simctl shutdown <id>; xcrun simctl erase <id>; xcrun simctl bootstatus <id> -b` before `xcodebuild test`. Let `bootstatus -b` finish booting: an `xcodebuild` started right after `erase` failed to launch the test host and then hung. macOS has no `timeout`; cap runs with `perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV' xcodebuild …`.  ## Build (macOS) — IMPORTANT, use Xcode MCP not CLI
CLI `xcodebuild -destination 'platform=macOS'` only works **unsigned** (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`) for compile checks. A signed/runnable macOS build fails with **"No Accounts: Add a new account"** — the CLI can't reach Xcode's Apple ID to mint Mac provisioning profiles.  To build/run/sign for macOS: 1. Open the project in **Xcode.app** (`open -a Xcode <project>`), which has [redacted-person]'s account. 2. **Set the run destination to "My Mac" in the Xcode toolbar manually** — the Xcode MCP has no tool to set scheme/destination; `BuildProject` builds whatever the toolbar is set to. 3. Build via MCP `BuildProject` (verify tab with `XcodeListWindows`). First My-Mac build auto-creates Mac provisioning for all 3 bundle ids.  - Unsigned compile check (fast, no account): `xcodebuild ... -destination 'platform=macOS' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build` - macOS entitlements are **separate files** wired via `CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS[sdk=macosx*]` (App Sandbox + network.client + files.user-selected + iCloud + App Group); iOS entitlements untouched. - Cross-platform helpers in `Theme.swift`: `inlineNavigationTitle()`, `.trailingAction`, `macSheetFrame()` (the last fixes `List`-in-sheet collapsing to blank on macOS).
 ## Project Format  Uses Xcode 16+ `PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup` (objectVersion 77). Files auto-sync — no manual pbxproj edits needed. SourceKit may report false "Cannot find type" errors across files; ignore if `xcodebuild` succeeds.  ## Architecture  - **SwiftData** for persistence. `ModelContainer.shared` in `ModelContainer+Shared.swift` — shared by app, widget, and share extension via App Group. - **Foundation Models** for on-device AI. All AI in `QuoteAIService.swift` using `@Generable` types + `LanguageModelSession`. - **Theme** in `Theme.swift` — fonts, warm background modifier, appearance setting enum, UIKit appearance setup.
- **Minimal networking** — enrichment (`Services/Enrichment/`, [redacted-project]#35) searches Wikiquote, Wikipedia and, when the build carries a key, Google Books; DuckDuckGo is gone. Wikipedia API for author photos. No user accounts or server dependencies. Seed data imported from bundled JSON. - **Google Books key** — never committed. Put `GOOGLE_BOOKS_API_KEY = <key>` in `Config/Secrets.xcconfig` (gitignored; included by `Config/[redacted-project].xcconfig`, the project's base configuration). It reaches the app and share extension as the Info.plist key `GoogleBooksAPIKey`; without it, enrichment skips Google Books.  ## Architecture map — `docs/architecture/`  `docs/architecture/runtime.html` is this repo's runtime architecture: the [redacted-project] app with its in-app browser and source review, its share extension and widget, the shared SwiftData store, CloudKit sync, and the enrichment APIs. Each box links to the file and lines it came from. `runtime.architecture.json` is its source, pinned to one commit in `meta.repository.revision`.  The map compresses the page reader, evidence windows and model fallback branches; author-cache and seed-import internals are not expanded.  Maps in this folder:
 - `runtime.html` (architecture): the runtime map described above. - `share-capture.html` (sequence): capturing a quote through the share extension: text or URL, on-device AI extraction, save to the shared store, then app backfill, enrich, and the widget pick.  - Read the map before structural work, then confirm against the code. It is correct only as of its pinned commit. - When a change moves a box or an edge, regenerate it with the `archify` skill: from `docs/architecture/`, run `node [redacted-path] finalize architecture runtime.architecture.json runtime.html --repo-root <repo> --quality showcase --json`, then commit the JSON and the HTML only.  Introduced by [[redacted-project]#1589]([redacted-url]).  ## Conventions
 - Use `SwiftUI.ForEach` (module-qualified) when iterating `@Model` types to avoid ambiguity. - Use `.warmBackground()` on all List views, `.warmBackground(plain: false)` on all Form views. - Use `.quoteBody` / `.quoteDisplay` / `.quoteAttribution` fonts for quote content. - `AccentColor` asset doesn't work on iOS 26 beta — use explicit `.tint()` on ContentView instead. - **Team + identifiers (2026-09-11):** all targets sign under [redacted-project] Ltd `5W6HCF649V`. The App Group is `group.com.example.[redacted-project].store` and the iCloud container `iCloud.com.example.[redacted-project].store` — the un-suffixed ids are owned by the old team `76H34XPVF9` and Apple refuses them for the new team (App Group / iCloud container ids are global across teams, and iCloud container ids can never be deleted). Data under the old ids is not reachable by this build. The one-time migration is **done** (2026-09-15, [redacted-project]#32/#33): 115 [redacted-project] restored on [redacted-person]'s iPhone under the `.store` ids via the devicectl App-Group pull + the app's Restore from Backup (memory: pull-ios-appgroup-data-via-devicectl). - **Xcode on the [redacted-host] (2026-09-29):** release Xcode 27.0 (27A266a) at `/Applications/Xcode-27.0.0.app`; the beta and 26.5 are gone. `xcode-select` may still point at Command Line Tools, so pass `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-27.0.0.app/Contents/Developer` (bare `xcrun simctl` fails otherwise). Device builds need `-allowProvisioningUpdates` the first time so Xcode registers the ids under the new team. - **macOS push entitlement key (CloudKit live sync):** macOS uses `com.apple.developer.aps-environment`, NOT the iOS-form `aps-environment`. The iOS key is invalid on macOS and is **silently stripped at signing** — the signed Mac app then carries no push entitlement and never gets CloudKit silent-push change notifications (sync still works on launch/poll, just not live). Verify with `codesign -d --entitlements :- <App>.app`. The macOS entitlements are a separate file (`*-macOS.entitlements`), so the iOS file being correct doesn't cover the Mac. - **Schema changes vs CloudKit (2026-09-29, [redacted-project]#36):** the shared container is CloudKit-backed (`cloudKitDatabase: .automatic`), and SwiftData does not support a custom `MigrationStage` on a CloudKit store — opening an upgraded store fails and the app terminates at launch. Schema changes must be additive-only lightweight changes, or (while the CloudKit Production schema is undeployed, [redacted-project]#28) a reset of the Development environment plus a backup restore. Tests that disable CloudKit for data safety do not exercise this path: any schema change must be checked against the CloudKit-backed container configuration, not only an in-memory/no-CloudKit store. - **Verifying CloudKit deletes:** the app uses **soft delete** (`Quote.softDelete` sets `deletedAt`; rows are retained ~30 days for recovery and hidden from the main list). When checking delete propagation in the SwiftData store, inspect `ZDELETEDAT` — do NOT use `COUNT(*)`/row presence, since a correctly-propagated soft-delete leaves the row in place.
- **Never touch `UIPasteboard.general` (or `NSPasteboard`) from an automated test (2026-09-16, [redacted-project]#46):** a real pasteboard read in the unit-test host raises the system "would like to paste from [redacted-project]" permission dialog with nobody to dismiss it, and the whole `xcodebuild test` run hangs until the process is killed. Clipboard code takes an injectable `ClipboardReading`; tests use the fake. - **`axe` / `idb` on Xcode 27 (2026-09-16, [redacted-project]#54; still true on the 27.0 release):** both fail with `SimulatorKit.framework … does not exist` because Xcode 27 ships it under `Contents/SharedFrameworks/` while the tools hardcode `Contents/Developer/Library/PrivateFrameworks/`. Bridged on this [redacted-host] with a symlink at the old path pointing to the new one (outside the repo, reversible; created by the #54 research agent). A fresh Xcode install loses it; recreate the symlink before simulator automation. The release bundle has no `Contents/Developer/Library/PrivateFrameworks/` directory at all, so `mkdir -p` it first (recreated 2026-09-29). - **Device logs over Wi-Fi are unreliable (2026-09-16, [redacted-project]#47):** `idevicesyslog -n -u <udid>` from this [redacted-host] drops the stream after roughly 10 s, so a live capture around a user action usually misses it; four attempts got one 9-second window. Read device logs over USB, or skip the measurement. The clipboard analysis logs `analyzeClipboard took N ms (prewarmed: Bool, chars: N)` under subsystem `com.example.[redacted-project]`, category `ClipboardAnalysis`, for whenever a USB read is possible. Also: `xcrun devicectl … process launch` and `copy from` need the phone unlocked and it auto-locks within a minute; ask [redacted-person] to unlock right before the call, not before a multi-step plan.  ## Swift Navigation (xcode-index-mcp)  Compiler-accurate Swift navigation (call sites + definitions) via Xcode's IndexStore — more reliable than `rg` for "who calls X" / "where is X defined" across the app target, share extension, and tests.
- **Tools** (`mcp__xcode-index-mcp__*`): `load_index`, `symbol_occurrences` (file+line →   USR), `get_occurrences` (USR+roles → all occurrences), `search_pattern`. - **Param names are camelCase**: `projectName`, `filePath`, `lineNumber`, `usr`, `roles`   (snake_case like `project_name`/`line` fails schema validation). **Call   `load_index("[redacted-path]")` once before querying.** `load_index` raises   a harmless pydantic warning on its *output* (it returns `{available: true}` against a   bool-typed result schema) — it still succeeds; ignore it. - **Pass the repo PATH, not a name.** [redacted-project] builds 5+ `[redacted-project]-*` DerivedData folders   (one per git worktree + export/import dirs). The resolver matches the folder whose   info.plist WorkspacePath sits directly in the path you pass, so pass the absolute repo
  root: `[redacted-path]` for main, or a worktree root   (`…/.worktrees/<name>`) to query that worktree. Passing the bare name `"[redacted-project]"`   falls back to legacy name-matching and picks an arbitrary worktree — don't. Resolution is   deterministic from the workspace path (verified: deleting + rebuilding the folder   regenerates the same DerivedData hash). - **Multi-target files have one USR per module — union them.** A file compiled into several   targets (app + share ext + widget ext) produces a *distinct USR per target*, with the   module name mangled in (e.g. `QuoteAIService` → `s:9[redacted-project]…`, `s:5share…`,   `s:20quotewidgetExtension…`). `symbol_occurrences` resolves to **one arbitrary** USR, so a   single `get_occurrences` returns only that target's hits (the share USR gives just 4). To
  get the true total, collect every USR for the symbol and **union `get_occurrences` across   all of them** — `QuoteAIService` = 1 def + 9 refs = 10, spread 6/3/0 across the three   targets. - **Cross-check `rg` against `get_occurrences`, not `search_pattern`.** The union-of-USR   `get_occurrences` is the compiler-accurate set and correctly excludes substring /   string-literal false matches (e.g. `QuoteAIServiceTests`, an `@Suite("QuoteAIService…")`   literal): `rg "QuoteAIService"` = 12 hits, USR union = 10. `search_pattern` does **not**   exclude those — it surfaces the test symbols too — so don't compare against it. - **File paths**: find with `rg -n`, pass the **absolute** path matching the root you loaded. - **Index reflects the last CLEAN build of that root.** If `load_index` says the store isn't
  found, build the [redacted-project] scheme from that root. Incremental rebuilds can leave stale   duplicate records (IndexStore doesn't purge moved-line units) — wrong line numbers or   dropped refs mean you need a **clean** rebuild, not an incremental one. - **Toolchain**: service built with the Xcode that builds [redacted-project]' index (26.5,   `/Applications/Xcode.app`). Change the default Xcode → rebuild   `[redacted-path]` (`swift build`) under that `DEVELOPER_DIR`. - **Scope**: registered LOCAL to this repo only. - **Path-mode resolver is a local patch** to the Block clone (SymbolProvider.swift),   mirroring how SourceKit-LSP disambiguates by build path.
